story_title: As an Event Organiser, I want to create an event request containing my event requirements so that ConnectSphere has the information needed to begin planning my event.

acceptance_criteria.text: The Event Organiser can enter an event name and purpose.
The Event Organiser can enter an event description.
The Event Organiser can specify the proposed date and time.
The Event Organiser can specify expected attendance.
The Event Organiser can specify venue, accessibility, equipment and registration requirements.
An event can be organised into multiple sessions, each with its own timing, expected attendance, venue and equipment requirements (e.g. a multi-day conference with different rooms per day).
The system validates required information before allowing submission.
A newly created incomplete request is identifiable as a draft.

open_questions: Every case logs in as the seeded organiser rachel.ng@meridianfina.com, so all testers share one "My events" list (drafts are private per account, not per tester) alongside her seeded events. Each tester puts their initials in every event name so their own drafts can be told apart, and no case relies on any seeded event or draft. Two testers who use the same initials can still open each other's draft by mistake, and drafts cannot be deleted from the app, so repeat runs add duplicate rows.

Cases that request equipment or tick facilities (TC10, TC11, TC13, TC24, TC28, TC29) need the seeded catalogue items ("4K Portable Projector", "Lavalier Wireless Mic", "High-density WiFi", "Wheelchair spaces") to exist. There is no screen to create equipment or facilities, so testers cannot set these up themselves. Accepted for now.

Cases that submit a request (TC04, TC07, TC09, TC18, TC33) end on the request's own page, which is not built yet and shows a 404 (Known Gaps, DOCUMENTATION.md; SPM-27/SPM-31). They check the result from "My events" instead. Once the detail page exists, these could also check what it shows.

Not written as manual cases because the UI cannot reach them: the server refusing a single-session list, refusing the same item in two sessions, and the submit-time check "Missing: session N expectedAttendance" (the form's own validation always stops these first). They are covered by unit tests in validation.test.ts, and were checked over HTTP during development.

SPM-23-TC13 was rewritten in this update: it still described a rejection message that can no longer appear (the equipment picker now hides already-chosen items, per the 2026-09-18 change). SPM-24-TC13 was fixed then; the SPM-23 copy was missed. TC10, TC11 and TC14 were also reworked to "Save draft, then reopen", because the details they checked were only visible on the unbuilt request page; TC11 and TC14 previously had no login or event name, so they could not have been run as written.
